title: Border policy graph for residency strictness and tenant-scoped exemptions
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Design and implement a policy-graph based routing constraint engine that enforces data residency strictness for EU-bound requests while supporting tenant-scoped exemptions. The engine will be used at the request ingress to decide regional routing, tiered routing eligibility, and whether to allow annotated exceptions (tenant permits). It must emit auditable decisions, be performant under high QPS, and support runtime updates to policies without restarts.
acceptance_criteria: Policy graph schema v1 defined and documented in Confluence
Runtime policy evaluator (PDP) deployed behind routing layer with <2ms median decision latency in load test
Routing decisions include: region target, allowed variants, fallback model family, and audit reason
Tenant exemption tokens evaluated and validated; exemptions are scoped to customer id + timebox
End-to-end tests for EU-residency requests where (a) compliant routing is enforced, (b) tenant exemptions are honored, (c) fallback model variant used when primary region unavailable
Audit logs written to centralized event stream with schema fields: request_id, tenant_id, decision, policy_id, evaluated_at
Canary rollout plan executed and monitoring shows no increase in 5xx or 99p latency
technical_notes: Policy graph nodes: CONDITION, DECISION, FALLBACK, EXEMPTION_CHECK, LOG
Conditions include request.region_hint, tenant.attributes.residency_requirement, account_tier, consent_flags
Exemption model: signed tenant permit JWT (short TTL) + server-side nonce lookup for revocation
PDP should be implemented in Rust for low-latency inline evaluation; library exported as gRPC service for the router
Cache policy decisions for 30s keyed by (tenant_id, routing_key, request_prefix_hash) with invalidation on policy update
Fallback path: when EU capacity unavailable, map to geo-compliant model variant in nearby region (e.g., eu-west -> eu-north) or degrade to restricted-hosted with additional audit
Security: policy updates signed by ops CI and require KMS-backed verification before loading
